answer: Latency-Anchored Edge Weighting. Each agent’s influence equals the inverse of its median round-trip latency to a rotating zephyr of geographic anchor nodes; edges spanning implausibly short paths gain weight only after repeated, time-stamped traversal. A sybil cluster must physically distribute nodes and sustain real relay hops to fake proximity, raising its per-identity cost to colocated hardware, bandwidth, and upkeep. Honest agents near a meadow region converge naturally, while a lone pearl of high-weight identity cannot be cloned cheaply.
